observations: G282 F-Droid GET timed out after 250.015 seconds with no accepted APK; stderr reports 73,482,186 bytes received while retained partial is only 1,765,376 bytes, so transfer and residual accounting differ and neither is accepted.
Pilot official GitHub API returned Element X digest/size equal to registered SHA/size in 0.932 seconds; Element Classic gplay digest/size differed from registered F-Droid SHA/size in 0.598 seconds.
inference: A digest-first route can cheaply identify an exact-byte alternate channel or reject same-version mismatches before committing to a large GET.
hypothesis: For future publisher releases exposing SHA-256, metadata equality will reduce wasted download attempts without increasing false raw admissions, provided full payload hash and signer checks remain mandatory.
unknown: Whether the alternate Element X endpoint completes an actual GET
Whether the downloaded bytes and signer match the API digest
How often other publishers expose suitable digest metadata
discarded_action: Blind repeat of the timed-out F-Droid GET or reuse of its partial, anchored to G282 RESULT; the prior attempt has no full artifact identity and cannot establish progress toward admission.
causal_chain: 250-second unsuccessful transfer -> exact alternate channel was not tested by SHA before GET -> publisher digest/size comparison to upstream lock -> avoid wrong-flavor or unsupported large transfer attempts -> measure metadata time and later complete-payload SHA success.
applicability: Only exact registered package/version/artifact SHA+size with publisher-controlled release API digest; metadata gate does not confer raw, static, blackbox, graph or device credit.
risk: Publisher API metadata is mutable and may be absent; pin response identity at download time and hash full payload. A mismatched digest means a separate candidate, not historical artifact substitution.
